title: Image prompts and dimensions got more predictable
summary:
The week was about making image requests take the right path, use predictable settings, and leave clearer signals when work queued up.

Image prompt enhancement now has its own route through the text API. Requested dimensions map to the closest supported aspect ratio, and short prompts honor an explicit `enhance=false`. Prompt sanitization also now strips non-ASCII characters before text reaches the image backend, which changes how accented prompts are handled.

Prompt-enhancement requests bypass the ordinary text per-IP queue, while ordinary text requests now have a concurrency limit of one per IP and a longer pause after generation errors. On the image side, queue counts now come from Flux workers, queueing events reach feed listeners again, and worker tracking and routing were extended across Flux, Turbo and translation services. Flux also retains more generation steps under moderate load.

Image operations moved to asynchronous file I/O, the cache gained a 500,000-entry limit, and debug logs and progress tracking replaced much of the previous console output. Tests now cover generation, processing, caching, prompts and queues. JSON mode also accepts boolean `json: true`, and image safe-mode checks were refined.

A new SDK & Libraries section in the README and website showcase points to React and Python integrations. AI-Bloom joined the project list, Pollinations Gallery was marked as new, and Sur switched from Claude to OpenAI.
